comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar within full-service restaurant at 970–974 Valencia, 66 meters away, same NCT-VALENCIA zoning, filed 2010. This is a use decision (CUA) for a bar component in a restaurant concept.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Application was withdrawn before the Planning Commission hearing. Withdrawn CUAs for bar uses on this corridor suggest that either the applicant could not meet conditions during pre-hearing discussions or faced hurdles that made the project unviable.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for a bona fide eating place (Type 41 beer/wine) with live entertainment and arts activities at 2519 Mission, 210 meters away, NCT-MISSION zoning, filed 2019. Change of use from retail to restaurant with entertainment.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Withdrawn before hearing despite being a Type 41 restaurant with entertainment—not even a bar use. The withdrawal of an eating-place-with-entertainment CUA signals that live entertainment combined with alcohol in this neighborhood faces scrutiny even at the restaurant level.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral for continuation of existing Type 41 license at 1007–1017 Valencia, 45 meters away, NCT-VALENCIA zoning, approved 2008. Restaurant with beer/wine on the same block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approval explicitly states 'does not establish a new bar use at subject location.' Planning drew a bright line: continuing a Type 41 restaurant license is permitted, but it does not authorize a change to bar use. This distinction is critical for 995 Valencia's proposed conversion from restaurant to bar.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving a Place of Entertainment permit at 998 Valencia (31 meters away, same NCT-VALENCIA zoning) as accessory to retail use in 2014. POE approved under the 1/3-floor-area rule for accessory entertainment.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Entertainment Commission POE referral approved by Planning when entertainment is accessory (≤1/3 of floor area) to a principal permitted use. A bar with live entertainment as a co-equal or primary use would not qualify for this accessory pathway and would need a full CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving POE for Restaurant and Nighttime Entertainment uses at 2512 Mission (152 meters, NCT-MISSION), decided 2020. Combined restaurant + entertainment venue (Arcana).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved the Entertainment Commission referral for a restaurant with nighttime entertainment use. As an agency referral it shows Planning permits entertainment when paired with a restaurant, but it does not test whether a bar-primary use would receive Commission approval.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Public Convenience or Necessity referral for a nonprofit theater with accessory bar at 2519 Mission (210 meters, NCT-MISSION), approved 2021. ABC undue-concentration area requiring city PCN finding.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning recommended approval of the PCN finding for an accessory bar in a nonprofit theater. The record confirms this block is in an ABC undue-concentration area requiring PCN findings, and Planning will support them when the bar is accessory to arts/culture uses.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving POE and Extended Hours Premises permits at 2500 Mission (145 meters, NCT-MISSION), decided July 2026—the most recent entertainment approval on this corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved Entertainment Commission permits for late-night entertainment (after 2 a.m.) as recently as four months ago.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 1999 for a full-service restaurant/bar with outdoor seating at 2526–2548 Mission (159 meters, NCT-MISSION). Approved bar use in the Mission corridor, though pre-dating the SUD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Bar use was approved as part of a restaurant in NCT-MISSION in 1999 with no extracted conditions, but this predates the 2008 Mission Alcohol SUD restrictions. It shows historical precedent for bar approvals but does not reflect current SUD constraints.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral for Limited Live Performance permit at 1034 Valencia (94 meters, NCT-VALENCIA) as accessory to a video store, denied 2015. Rare denial of an entertainment accessory use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning denied an LLP permit even as an accessory use to retail. While the record does not state a reason, the denial shows that entertainment permits are not rubber-stamped even at the Limited Live Performance level, and discretionary review or compatibility concerns can block approval.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 2007 to convert from bar use to retail at 2410–2412 Mission (193 meters, NCT-MISSION). Bar-to-retail conversion, showing a bar use existed but was replaced.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This CUA approved the elimination of a bar use, converting it to retail. It confirms that bar uses have existed in NCT-MISSION but provides no guidance on approval standards for new bars, since the use was being removed rather than established.

filing_playbook.action: Register for the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate with the Treasurer & Tax Collector and file the Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The Business Account Number (BAN) is issued within 1–5 days. The fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 for under $100k, $95 for under $250k). File the FBN statement in person or by mail with photo ID, then publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with SF Planning to confirm the Mission Alcohol SUD license-transfer requirement and identify an available Type 42 license from a bar within the SUD.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the assigned project planner (or request one through the Planning intake desk) and ask: (1) Can you confirm that a new bar at 995 Valencia must use an ABC Type 42 license transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD, not a new license from ABC? (2) Will Planning provide a letter confirming this requirement so I can engage a license broker? (3) What good-neighbor conditions (security plan, hours, sound, capacity) should I plan for in the CUA application? Bring the concept profile and a draft floor plan showing the bar area, kitchen and entertainment space.

filing_playbook.action: File the ABC transfer application with a signed lease, a seller's permit, and a request for a Public Convenience or Necessity finding.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the ABC person-to-person and premises-to-premises transfer application at abc.ca.gov with the signed lease, the entity formation documents, the seller's permit (obtained from CDTFA), and the $1,000–$1,600 license fee. Given the undue-concentration density (51 on-sale licenses within 1,000 ft), expect ABC to require a PCN finding. ABC's standard 60-day timeline.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Submit the DPH plan check application for the limited kitchen and bar, and the building permit application to DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, both routed to Planning, Fire, PUC and DPH.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Through the DPH portal submit two sets of scaled kitchen and bar drawings, interior/exterior photos, a menu describing the limited cooking (small plates, charcuterie, panini), and an equipment list (panini press, refrigeration, three-compartment sink, hand sinks). Pay the plan-check fee ($828–$2,207 depending on review hours). In parallel, file the building permit application through PermitSF with architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the bar area, the limited kitchen, the entertainment space, ADA upgrades, and any structural or MEP work. The permit will be routed to Planning (for CUA conformance), DPH (for health plan check), Fire (for occupancy and hood suppression) and PUC (for FOG interceptor). Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% construction completion.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline spans 9–22 months and is driven by the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to hearing plus 30-day appeal period), the ABC Type 42 license transfer from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD (90–180 days, extended to 120–270 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required due to undue concentration), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days including posting and hearing). The building permit with change of use adds 14–120 days for plan review. The cost range covers city fees only: CUA application (~$3,100, CPI-adjusted), POE application ($2,708), ABC license transfer application fee ($1,000–$1,600, not including the purchase price of the license from the selling bar, which is a private transaction often costing $20k–$100k+ in saturated markets), DPH plan check ($828–$2,207), Health Permit to Operate application ($470), building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), and business registration ($55–$700 depending on gross receipts). The license purchase price, construction costs, architect and acoustic engineer fees, broker fees, and insurance premiums are not government fees and are not included in this range. The critical path is: (1) identify and escrow an available Type 42 license from a bar within the SUD (2–4 months), (2) file and win the CUA (4–10 months), (3) close the license transfer and obtain the PCN finding (3–9 months, overlapping with construction), (4) obtain the POE permit (2–4 months, after CUA approval), (5) complete tenant improvements and pass final inspections (2–4 months). Start the license search and the CUA application in parallel immediately after the pre-application meeting with Planning. The total timeline assumes no appeals, no CUA continuances, and that an available Type 42 license from within the SUD can be located and escrowed; if no license is available or if the seller withdraws, the project cannot proceed under current SUD rules.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the Valencia Street NCT district where a bar is a conditional use requiring a Conditional Use Authorization (CUA). The site is inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which permits bars only as conditional uses and requires the ABC license to be transferred from another bar within the SUD—a new license from ABC cannot be used. An active Type 41 license (Sarita's Grill & Beer, issued Nov 2023) establishes the current use as a Restaurant; converting to a bar is a change of use. The block is saturated: 24 food/drink businesses and 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, 51 licenses within 1,000 ft, triggering ABC's undue-concentration proxy and likely requiring a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the City. Only 3 dated use decisions in 10 years within 1,000 ft—too few to compute an approval rate—but one was a 2011 CUA at this address upgrading a Type 41 to Type 47, approved without conditions.
